Roadmap & Data — How We Move Forward

The foundation (data + engine) is built. From here the work is about the experience on top and deepening the data, in clear phases.

The phases, in detail

  • Phase 1 — the builder workspace: the chosen interface direction (Section 16 of the main report), the opportunity heatmap, the full 7-step flow, decomposed confidence, the Evidence Explorer, and — if approved — the grounded AI co-pilot.
  • Phase 2 — scale & monitor: extend the pricing engine beyond the 5 modelled Amman submarkets to more governorates as data depth allows; add investor-memo generation and "what changed since last month?" action-alerts.
  • Phase 3 — delivery: secure hosting, access control, and hand-over to the client.

The data-enrichment wave — tiered, so effort goes where it pays

For each area, we first generate the specific web queries our own data says are missing, then fetch in three tiers:

  • Tier 1 — search & APIs for quick, structured facts (prices, amenities, news)
  • Tier 2 — browser automation for pages that need clicking, scrolling, or maps (JS-heavy sites, paginated results)
  • Tier 3 — VPN for geo-blocked official sources: the remaining DLS monthly reports and the official GAM zoning / FAR (both currently unreachable from outside Jordan)

Per-area geographic enrichment then captures orientation, city-view potential by height, hills / river / greenery, noise vs calm, safety, and nearby transit — the inputs the pricing factors need.

How we confirm the data is right (not just claimed)

We run independent web cross-checks against authoritative sources. In the latest pass, all six headline figures were corroborated (6/6):

FigureVerdict
Construction cost ~157–175 JD/m²CONFIRMED as a FLOOR (turnkey ~220–1,100 by class)
DLS trading volume (2025 ~7.18bn JD)CONFIRMED & CURRENT
West-Amman prestige pricesCONFIRMED tier
BRT delivered / Metro speculativeCONFIRMED
Aqaba ASEZ ownership regimeCONFIRMED
Population ~11.4MCONFIRMED (context)

Verification annotates our data (adds a last-checked date and flags any conflict) — it never silently overwrites a value.

Map & visualization options (decision-relevant)

Better maps directly power the terrain and view analysis, so this is a real choice with a budget angle:

OptionWhat it addsCost
MapLibre + OpenStreetMap RECOMMENDED BASEFree base; great for our overlays; no lock-inFree
Satellite / aerial layerActual terrain, hills, greenery — powers the terrain & view factorsLow
3D terrain / elevationCity-view potential by height — the high-floor premiumLow–moderate
Google MapsRichest places + Street ViewPay-per-use + lock-in
MapboxPolished; satellite + 3D built inFreemium

Recommendation: free MapLibre/OSM base + satellite + 3D terrain for the analysis; Google/Mapbox optional later; the provider is kept replaceable.

Hosting options (for a non-technical client)

  • The client's own company cloud / IT — if they have a cloud account and DevOps, we deploy there (most control, uses existing contracts)
  • A small managed host — we set up and run it on a modest managed service (simplest for the client; low monthly cost)

Either way the platform is delivered with secure access; the choice is about who operates it and the budget.

Latest-data-first commitment: we prioritise 2026-to-date data. Older data is kept only as trend and context, and it is always vintage-labelled — nothing stale is ever presented as current.
Already banked (recent wins): official construction cost (~157 JD/m² Kingdom, ~175 JD/m² Greater Amman) which fixed the maximum-land-price calculator; official Aqaba zoning & foreign-ownership rules; and DLS annual transaction history.

Explicitly Phase 2 (not now)

  • Deeper statistical / machine-learning pricing once transaction depth allows
  • Automated investor memos and action-alert monitoring
  • Expanding full price-modelling to many more areas
  • Recovering the geo-blocked official zoning & the missing DLS months via the VPN route
